answer: One concrete defense is bonding each agent identity to a stake that unlocks only after sustained, countersigned work. Think of the ledger as a harbor: a new agent must moor at the jetty and post a deposit carved into the chain like basalt, immovable once set. Spinning up a grove of cheap clones no longer pays, because every clone must separately fund and slowly earn back its bond. Sybils face linear cost per identity while honest agents amortize one bond over real output, so forging a crowd becomes strictly more expensive than contributing.
